raw_response:
I'm 74, never went to school, can't read a single character. I came back to farming this land 20 years ago when my legs got too tired for construction work in Handan. My wife is 71, she still bends down to hoe. My son works in a shop in the county town and sends a little money home, but I don't ask him for farm money — this is my responsibility. Two mu is tiny, I know, but it's what we have. Every jin of fertilizer and every yuan for pumping water has to be counted carefully.

Cotton is what I know. I've grown it on these 2 mu every year since I started. I plant when the elm trees leaf out, around April 20. I don't use a calendar — the trees tell me. For seed, I saved the best bolls from last year's crop, kept them dry in the house. Buying new hybrid seed costs 60 or 70 yuan per mu, and Old Li down the road says it's better, but I've done fine with my own seed and saving that money means I have cash for medicine if my back acts up.

For fertilizer, I put down one bag of that 15-15-15 compound stuff per mu at planting — about 50 jin per bag. That's what I've always done. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, I spread half a bag of urea per mu, about 25 jin. I tried putting more urea two years ago and the plants grew too tall and fell over in the wind, so I won't do that again. I can't afford more anyway.

I irrigate twice from my well — once when the flowers open, and once in August when the bolls are swelling. Pumping costs electricity, so I don't water more. If the rains come good, maybe only once. Old Zhang waters three times but his son has a factory job and sends him more money.

Pesticides — cotton always has bugs. I spray three times: once for aphids when the plants are small, once for bollworm when it gets hot, once for red spider in late summer. I also spray herbicide once before planting to keep the weeds down. The shop in town sells me small bottles and I mix them in my backpack sprayer. My wife carries the water buckets — my back can't lift heavy loads anymore.

For tillage, I hire Old Wang's small tractor to plow — he charges 30 yuan per mu. Then I break the clods with a hoe and make the rows by hand. Planting I do row by row, dropping seeds by hand. It's slow but I don't have a planter and hiring one for 2 mu isn't worth it.

Labor is mostly family. My wife and I do the planting, hoeing, and spraying. For picking, cotton needs many hands — the bolls open at different times and you have to pick three or four rounds. We do the first rounds ourselves, then hire two women from the east end of the village for about 5 or 6 days total. Pay them 80 yuan a day plus lunch. That's my biggest cash expense, but without them we'd lose cotton to rain and rot.

Last year was dry and I only got about 400 jin of seed cotton per mu. A normal year I get 450 to 500 jin per mu. This spring the soil looks okay, so I hope for 440 jin per mu — that's about 220 of those kg units the buyer uses. Cotton price has been around 7.5 yuan per jin, so if I get 880 jin total from 2 mu, that's about 6,600 yuan. After costs, maybe 5,500 yuan left. Not much, but it keeps us going.
